paragraphs.text: A new commission to preach again to his countrymen, which he had not done since Eze 24:27. {See Trapp on "Eze 24:27"}
paragraphs.anchor: Again the word of the Lord came unto me, saying.

paragraphs.text: I say, "of thy people"; for I can scarce find in my heart to own them, they be so bad.
paragraphs.anchor: Speak to the children of thy people.

paragraphs.text: The sword is of God’s sending; {Eze 14:17} and whencesoever it cometh, it is bathed in heaven. {Isa 34:5} Think the same of any other public calamity, {Amo 3:6} and therefore frame to a patient and peaceable behaviour under it. Among philosophers the most noted sect for patience was that of the Stoics, who ascribed all to fate.
paragraphs.anchor: When I bring the sword upon a land.

paragraphs.text: Hence the ancients {a} infer that a bishop must preach, and that Praelati officium est sollicitudo non celsitudo. He taketh upon him the office of a constant preacher, saith Gregory, that undertaketh to be a minister.
{a} Clemens, Bernard.
The blame shall rest wholly upon himself. Not to be warned is both a just presage and desert of destruction.
paragraphs.anchor: His blood shall be upon his own.

paragraphs.text: Foresight is the best means of prevention.
This is a dismal kind of death, far worse than that of dying in prison, or of dying in a ditch.
paragraphs.anchor: He is taken away in his iniquity.

paragraphs.text: As the watchman’s hand.] By whose treachery, or indiligence at least, he miscarried.
{See Trapp on "Eze 3:17"}
{See Trapp on "Eze 3:18"}
{See Trapp on "Eze 3:19"}

{a} But not well, while ye have hard thoughts of God and heavy thoughts of yourselves, as if your sins were unpardonable, and that ye were already ruined beyond relief; whereas true repentance is a ready remedy, a plank after shipwreck, that would set you safe, and render you right again. This they had been told before, {Eze 18:25-32} but to little purpose: the word was not mingled with faith in their hearts, and did therefore run through them, {Heb 2:1} as water runs through a riven vessel.

Ita punimur ut pereamus. And so be punished and perish. This the prophet had threatened, {Eze 24:23} and they still stomachfully object it to him: it lay as hard meat, and they raise a cavil upon it, whereto the Lord answereth,
paragraphs.anchor: And we pine away in them.

paragraphs.text: {a} Refricat verba desperantium. Omnis restitutionis species et spes a Deo nobis praecisa est.

This is one of those precious places, those mellifluous honeycombs, which we should go on sucking towards heaven, as Samson once did towards his parents. {Jdg 14:9} Here, if anywhere, we may find "strong consolation." God, when he swears, desires certainly to be credited, saith Tertullian. {a} Oh happy we, for whose sakes God vouchsafeth to swear! and oh, thrice wretched we, if we believe not God, no, though he swear to us! Oh, saith Theodoret here, who can ever sufficiently admire the Lord’s great goodness, who, being so shamefully slighted by the sinful sons of men, doth yet swear his readiness to receive them graciously who have revolted grievously? Well might Nazianzen say that God delighteth in nothing so much as in man’s conversion and salvation: {b} φοβεισθαι βουλεται, ου φονευσαι, saith Basil - i.e., he would we should fear him, not fall by his hand: Redire nos sibi, non perire desiderat, as Chrysologus phraseth it, return unto him, not "perish from the way." {Psa 2:12}
paragraphs.anchor: As I live, saith the Lord God, &c.

paragraphs.text: Turn ye must, or burn. See Eze 18:31-32.
{a} Lib. de Poenitent., cap. 4.
{b} Suffundere mavult sanguinem quam effundere. - Tertul.
The same as before, only with a proviso of perseverance in welldoing, for else all is lost. Non enim quaeruntur in Christianis initia sed finis, saith Jerome, The end is better than the beginning.
See on Eze 18:24.
paragraphs.anchor: When I shall say to the righteous.

paragraphs.text: As thinking that he hath thereby purchased a licence to commit iniquity.
paragraphs.anchor: If he trust to his own righteousness.

paragraphs.text: viz., Except thou repent; for that altereth the case. Penitence is almost as good as innocence.
These two parts make up true repentance.
paragraphs.anchor: If he turn from his sin and do.

paragraphs.text: Quod rapuit reddideret. The law for restitution, see Num 5:6-7.
paragraphs.anchor: Give again that he had robbed.

paragraphs.text: This is point blank against the doctrine of purgatory.
This was a second cavil of theirs. See Eze 33:10; Eze 18:25. Archesilas was surnamed Cavillator: so might these well have been.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet the children of the people say.

paragraphs.text: There is no equity at all in this causeless quarrel of theirs.
To set them down, if right reason would do it (and man should be mancipium rationis, a slave to reason), he repeateth what he hath said before.
Provided that he rest not in his righteousness, but learn to live by the faith of the Son of God. {Gal 2:20}
But therein ye lie, which is not the guise of God’s children. {Isa 63:8}
And so wring a testimony, if not from your mouths, yet from your consciences, of mine impartial justice; such as is that in Deu 32:4, "A God of truth, and without iniquity, just and right is he."
paragraphs.anchor: I will judge you every one after his ways.

paragraphs.text: Some read the eleventh year; and indeed it was wonder that such ill news came no sooner, for αι βλαβαι ποδωκεις, saith Sophocles.
{a} This God had promised. {Eze 24:26}
i.e., Sacked and burnt. This man spoke much in few.
{a} Superates tragis.
i.e., The Spirit of the Lord, which acted me and carried me out. {2Pe 1:21 1Co 12:3}
As God had promised. {Eze 24:27} And this happened before the messenger’s narration. This was much for the prophet’s honour.
See Eze 18:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Then the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Those poor few now left in the land. {2Ki 25:12; 2Ki 25:22 Jer 40:5-6} Surely they are poor, they are foolish, they have lost the fruit of their affliction; Miserrimi facti sunt et pessimi permanent, as Augustine saith of some in his time, They are nevertheless wicked for being wretched.
paragraphs.anchor: They that inhabit those wastes of the land of lsrael.

paragraphs.text: Bubbles of words. Antiquum obtinent. They are no changelings, not at all crest fallen.
{a} And no such one but that we may match him. Thus these proud hypocrites hit up their counter for a thousand pounds, and stand upon their comparisons without all shame or sense.
And here we will hold our own, for we are well worthy.
paragraphs.anchor: The land is given to us.

paragraphs.text: {a} Verba faecis populi recitat. Abrahae se conferre, imo praeferre audebant.

Which wicked Saul would not do, {1Sa 14:32-34} much less would righteous Abraham have done it, since it was against the light and letter of the law. {Gen 9:4 Lev 7:26 Deu 12:16} Nay, ye do worse things; and are you Abraham’s children, and heirs of the promised land, together with that faithful patriarch? I think not. See a like manner of reasoning, Mic 2:7 Joh 8:39. So the learned Linaker, having read our Saviour’s sermon in the mount, and considering how little it is lived among us, broke out into these words, Certainly either this is not gospel, or we are not right gospellers.
Vivitur ex rapto. He that hath the longest sword carrieth it among you: ye are also very revengeful, ready to say with him in the poet,
“ Virtus mihi numeri, et ensis
Quem teneo.
Dextra mihi deus, et telum quod missile libro. ”{ a}

This R. Solomon understandeth de venere obscaeniore. It is in the original, Ye women work abomination, as prostituting yourselves to an unnatural filthiness, as the casuists complain still of some Spanish courtezans. {b}
q.d., Ye shall be set up: what should you expect better than exilium et excitium, banishment and destruction?
paragraphs.anchor: And shall ye possess the land

paragraphs.text: {a} Caparene ap. Statum. Theb., 2. Mezent. ap. Virg. Aeneid, 10.
{b} Martin Vivald., in Candelab.

paragraphs.anchor: They that are in the wastes.

paragraphs.text: Or else of the famine, which is worse. When, where, and how this was fulfilled upon them, we read not; in Egypt likely, whither they went after Gedaliah’s death; if not sooner at home, as Jeremiah also had before prophesied. {Jer 42:13-14}
Heb., Desolation and desolation. God made clean work there; there was not a Jew left in the country. See Zec 7:14.
paragraphs.anchor: For I will lay the land most desolate.

paragraphs.text: By woeful experience.
These captives in Babylon, no whit better than those in Jewry.
Detracting from thee, and deriding thee.
Susurros miscentes clancularios; fearing lest any one behind them should hear them, they get the walls at their backs.
Thus they jeer; {a} and there are too many such scoffers at this day.
paragraphs.anchor: Come, I pray you, and hear.

paragraphs.text: {a} Uti otiosi et sauniones in foro facere solent.
Very goodly.
Very demurely, and, to see to, devoutly, taking up all the seats.
But they were as heartless in hearing, as they were listless in praying. {Eze 33:10}
Of the Athenians also it was said of old, that they knew well what was good and right, but would do neither.

Their heart is on their halfpenny, as we say; neither can the loadstone of God’s Word hale them one jot from the earth. It should be Sursum corda; up from the heart, but when many men’s bodies are in sacculis, in their purse, their hearts are in sacculis, in their purse, as Augustine complaineth; as serpents have their bodies in the water, their heads out of the water, so here; as those Gergesites, they more mind a swine sty than a sanctuary. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Their heart goeth after their covetousness.

paragraphs.text: {a} Haram domesticam arae Dominicae praefer.

Or, A love song. {a} The word leaves no more impression upon carnal men’s consciences than a sweet lesson upon the lute in the ear when it is ended, for then both the vocal and instrumental sweetness dissolve into the air and vanish into nothing. Happy was Augustine, who, coming to Ambrose to have his ears tickled, had his heart touched.
{a} Canticum amatorium. - Vatab.
See on Eze 2:5.
